Archive name validation normalizes the joined path and requires the destination plus path separator as prefix, rejecting absolute and platform-specific traversal names.

Dependency index parsing replaces the problematic URL regex with a bounded-count split on equals/whitespace, avoiding its ReDoS path.

WebDAV directory-browser Jinja environment enables select_autoescape instead of rendering listing data without HTML escaping.
DMS title-column content is escaped after Unicode normalization instead of returning raw user-controlled title text.
Querybook OAuth/Okta error callbacks HTML-escape the error query parameter before placing it in the returned h1 HTML.
Registers an after-request hook that sends X-Frame-Options: DENY, directly addressing the linked frame-embedding flaw.
HTTP request setup enables pycurl SSL_VERIFYPEER rather than explicitly disabling peer certificate verification.
Cloud-init sensitive metadata matching lowercases keys and nested key paths so mixed-case credential fields are not missed by redaction.
Cloud-init log-file setup reapplies its restricted 0640 mode instead of preserving a potentially world-readable preexisting file mode.
GraphQL mutation authentication catches invalid-token errors and returns a fixed validation message rather than exposing the internal exception.
Markdown CLI explicitly reads UTF-8 and ignores invalid sequences instead of crashing on attacker-supplied invalid bytes.
Markdown token processing handles absent children/attributes using conditional branches instead of attacker-triggerable assertions, addressing the null-assertion denial of service.
Streamlit error responses no longer reflect attacker-controlled paths or read errors into response HTML, removing the reflected XSS material.
Temporary download allocation changes from noncreating tempfile.mktemp to atomic tempfile.mkstemp, preventing precreation of the chosen path.
Image validation uses the temporary uploaded file directly instead of loading the entire file into an in-memory BytesIO, removing the disclosed memory-exhaustion copy.
Multipart header processing counts files and fields and raises before allocating beyond configured maxima, directly addressing unlimited multipart part resource consumption.

Canarytoken CSV history exports quote all fields and prefix exported values with an apostrophe, preventing spreadsheet formula interpretation of attacker-controlled incident data.
Peering Manager explicitly renders user templates through jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment rather than the unrestricted Environment.
Wiki snippet generation re.escape()s the search keyword before interpolating it into a regex, preventing user-defined pathological regex expressions.
Repository action lookup uses a queryset restricted to the requesting user's change permission rather than an unrestricted GitRepository lookup.
Refresh-token cleaning distinguishes None from an empty supplied token so empty-string requests cannot fall back to cookie credentials and skip the intended CSRF validation route.
Frigate rejects filenames longer than 1000 characters before invoking secure_filename's expensive Unicode normalization, bounding the disclosed denial-of-service input.
Social-auth lookup verifies the returned UID with Python's case-sensitive equality rather than trusting the database's case-insensitive collation.
EVTX upload storage uses secure_filename on the uploaded name before joining the destination, preventing arbitrary-path writes.
LocalFileStore normalizes the requested absolute path and requires commonpath to equal its root, rejecting keys that escape the root.
MLflow experiment creation explicitly rejects artifact URLs with fragments, closing the documented fragment-based path-validation bypass.
Solara keeps the trusted extension directory as send_from_directory's fixed base and supplies the user directory inside its relative filename, applying framework confinement to both components.
Sentry subprocess wrapper preserves an explicit empty env dict instead of replacing it with os.environ because it is falsy, preventing unintended environment disclosure.
Juju secret commands pass protected temporary-file references instead of literal secret content in argv, preventing secret exposure through command exceptions/process arguments.
Vectorizer no longer collects, returns or stores removed training terms as stop_words_, removing unnecessary retention of sensitive input tokens.
Devika PDF-download endpoint applies secure_filename to project_name before building its download path, correcting the PDF-download traversal advisory only.

followups.reason: Full function and module imports inspected: environment values are parsed with ast.literal_eval instead of eval, eliminating Python-expression execution while preserving literal conversion.

Each selected redirect of the request next parameter now calls safe_redirect. Companion helper was inspected: Django url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme with no external allowed hosts checks the URL and rejects unsafe targets to '/'. Helper source is separately required to match upstream and is preserved with the pair.

Complete redirect function inspected: the 303-to-GET branch clears the request body before the recursive request. Companion HTTPHeaderDict helper strips content-specific headers. Scope is this manager's GET-converting 303 path, not a claim about every redirect branch.

Full callers and middleware binding inspected. HorizonMiddleware.process_request binds request.user_logout to a helper that deletes _cached_user and calls request.session.flush(), replacing clear() without session-key rotation. The selected logout and stale-session paths now use that helper, matching the advisory's session fixation/reuse mechanism. Preserve the complete middleware function, including request-class binding, as upstream-verified companion evidence.

Full injection function and containment helper inspected. The previously raw join of user path now goes through realpath and requires the resolved target to start with realpath(fs) plus a slash before privileged mkdir/tee. This establishes the dot-dot traversal correction for CVE-2012-3360. The separately linked symlink CVE is not attributed here because unprivileged realpath cannot establish protection against root-only-readable links.

Complete authenticator function, imports and module assignments inspected. random_generator is explicitly random.SystemRandom(), and all sixteen authenticator bytes switch from random.randrange to that system-entropy generator. Attribute only weak authenticators/password hiding CVE-2013-0294, not the distinct sequential CreateID CVE-2013-0342.

Complete JSON filter and module escape-table binding inspected. Both QuerySet serialization and json.dumps converge on force_text(result).translate(_safe_js_escapes) before mark_safe. The actual table maps ampersand, less-than and greater-than to literal JSON Unicode escapes, preventing attacker-supplied script-closing markup from escaping the HTML script context described by CVE-2014-3994.

Full before/after functions and preserved GHSA-578p-fxmm-6229 advisory inspected. The advisory explicitly identifies 84c495da20a91640a1ca551ace17df7f3be644aa as introducing CVE-2024-26151. These pairs change decode_contents() to decode_contents(formatter=None), unescaping rather than preserving HTML entities. Their before/after vulnerability direction is reversed for an intended vulnerable-to-fixing pair; this is not a supported fix even though CVEfixes links the commit.

Full MjStyle.handler before/after inspected against the entity-unescaping advisory. This function adds selective > to > conversion for CSS child selectors after getContent(); it preserves CSS compatibility when the separate parser fix restores HTML escaping. The selected function does not contain the vulnerable general HTML-entity decoding operation, so it is not admitted as a vulnerable function merely because it shares the corrective commit.

Full nested parser and enclosing applyAttributes inspected against preserved GHSA-578p-fxmm-6229. Corrective commit 8d410b7a500703080bb14ed7e3d2663fe16767e6 removes formatter=None from decode_contents, retaining escaping in template content instead of turning entity-encoded attacker markup into HTML. Both selected functions contain this exact correction; the enclosing/nested overlap remains provenance-grouped, not independent vulnerability evidence.

Complete authentication function plus is_valid_hostname, is_valid_matrix_server_name and parse_server_name inspected. This selected commit replaces an existing hostname validator with a Matrix-server-name validator that accepts IPv4/IPv6 literals and optional validated ports; its commit message explicitly describes IPv6 compatibility. It does not add the advisory's missing origin validation or internal-address blacklist, and permits syntactically valid private addresses. Reject this compatibility pair as the CVE-2021-29431 mitigation rather than inferring relevance from inclusion in the advisory's multi-commit series.

Deeper review inspected each complete caller plus _inject_file_into_fs and _join_and_check_path_within_fs. These fixed metadata/key/network/password paths are not attacker-selected dot-dot paths, so CVE-2012-3360 cannot simply be assigned to all. Symlink containment depends on unprivileged os.path.realpath before root-privileged writes; root-only-readable guest links remain an explicit unresolved boundary. Retain outside admission pending precise CVE-2012-3361 conditions/fixing-direction evidence; do not describe the containment helper as establishing protection for every privileged symlink case.

Full SSLCA.build_request and subprocess imports inspected. The replacement constructs an argv list but leaves shell=True. On the referenced POSIX shell path, list elements after openssl become shell arguments rather than OpenSSL request arguments, so this does not establish a functioning intended CSR-generation fix. Do not equate list construction with shell=False or claim this function still has an exploitable injection without further evidence; retain as an explicit fixing-counterpart problem.

Full process_statistics caller and both async_run implementations inspected. Previously client-associated metadata arguments were joined into an os.system command. The caller now passes [notifier] + args to Trigger.async_run, whose subprocess.Popen receives the argv list without shell=True. pipes.quote is only used for diagnostic display. This removes shell interpretation in the advisory-named Trigger execution path; the complete helper is preserved separately.

Full DifferentHostFilter.host_passes and old/new lookup helpers inspected. Previously each hint UUID called compute_api.get through _affinity_host, so repeated IDs caused repeated API/database lookups. _all_hosts makes one compute_api.get_all call and builds a UUID-to-host map; the hint loop then uses dictionary lookup. This establishes removal of hint-count-proportional API calls for the advisory's DifferentHostFilter path, not a universal scheduler resource bound.

Full password-reset view and HttpRequest.get_host before/after inspected. The admin-site branch no longer passes raw HTTP_HOST into the reset domain override; get_host now rejects hostname delimiters including @, semicolon, slash and question mark with SuspiciousOperation. This blocks the username/password Host-header poisoning described by CVE-2012-4520. Scope is this delimiter validation, not a claim of complete modern ALLOWED_HOSTS enforcement.

Full aendern plus the advisory-named klauen/lesen callers inspected. lesen's one-argument branch forwards params.args[0] to aendern as the nickname, and klauen also invokes aendern. The vulnerable aendern SELECT interpolates nickname/item directly; the corrected SELECT passes both as separate SQLite bound parameters. The named-entry-point mismatch is resolved by this actual call chain, not by assuming every changed function shares the CVE.

Full default_dir, platform factories, directory selection and creation helpers inspected. The old cached/existing-directory paths accepted writability alone. The new POSIX path checks directory type, exact 0700 permissions, process ownership and non-symlink status, including cached paths; unsuitable candidates fall back to checked directories or atomic tempfile.mkdtemp. Admit for the insecure POSIX temporary-directory reuse mechanism. Windows does not receive POSIX ownership/mode checks, so equivalent Windows ACL guarantees are not asserted.

Full intermediate_dir and its reuse/creation helpers inspected. Previously a predictable existing user/Python intermediate directory was reused without ownership, mode or symlink validation. The replacement reuses only a check_dir-approved parent or creates a fresh parent with tempfile.mkdtemp, then creates the Python-version child under that restricted parent. POSIX ownership/0700/non-symlink checks establish the referenced insecure-directory correction; no Windows ACL equivalence or general race-freedom claim is made.

Full check_xsrf_cookie before/after inspected. This function compares a submitted token to the expected cookie token; the change decodes the new masked representation before comparison. It does not serialize a token into a compressed response or introduce the random presentation mask that addresses BREACH. This is compatibility with the separately corrected xsrf_token property, not a supported vulnerable response-generation function for CVE-2014-9720.

Full DatasetFilenameWrapper.__str__ and its constructor before/after inspected together. The constructor retains the original dataset as unsanitized while wrapping dataset accesses. __str__ deliberately switches to unsanitized.file_name to preserve the original filesystem filename, and its false_path return is unchanged. This selected method adds no sanitization of user-controlled template text; it is compatibility plumbing for the separate wrapper change, not itself the command-template injection correction.

Complete PUT, POST, _build_url and companion _request inspected against the Pulp public-key TLS advisory. These selected changes only forward ignore_prefix or alter URL-prefix assembly; PUT/POST are not the public-key GET path. No certificate verification operation/default changes in these functions. They support the migration of public-key retrieval elsewhere and are not vulnerable certificate-retrieval functions merely because they share its commit.

Full chroot fetch/put and execution helpers inspected. Previously shutil.copyfile resolved guest-controlled symlinks in the host filesystem after string-prefix path normalization. The replacement streams dd reads/writes through a helper whose default /bin/sh is launched after the chroot command and target root, so guest path and symlink resolution occurs inside the chroot. Admission is for CVE-2015-6240's isolation-boundary correction, not a claim of safe arbitrary shell filenames or complete transfer correctness.

Full jail fetch/put, removed host-side normalization/copy helpers and replacement command helpers inspected. Host shutil.copyfile followed guest-controlled links outside the jail. New transfers use dd launched by jexec with the jail identifier and /bin/sh -c, moving path resolution into the jail. Scope is the documented symlink isolation mechanism; unrelated shell-input or transfer implementation guarantees are not inferred.

Full zone fetch/put, removed host-copy helpers and zlogin command construction inspected. The corrected paths stream through dd executed by zlogin in the selected zone instead of resolving and copying guest paths in the host namespace. This addresses guest-symlink escape for CVE-2015-6240. The string-shell branch and other filename/transfer concerns are not certified safe by this source/advisory judgement.

Full exec_command implementations and extracted _buffered_exec_command/_generate_cmd bodies inspected for all three connection backends. The selected methods previously already launched the command through chroot/jexec/zlogin; the new helper preserves that execution behavior while enabling streamed file transfers elsewhere. These functions do not contain the host-side shutil.copyfile symlink sink addressed by CVE-2015-6240, so they are refactor-only pairs for this advisory.

Each complete filesystem/multifilesystem function, old _path property, new _filesystem_path property, imports and multifilesystem inheritance inspected. Previously slash replacement plus os.path.join could discard the base on Windows drive paths. path_to_filesystem sanitizes the logical path then rejects each component with a drive, head, dot or dot-dot before joining it below the configured base. All selected filesystem operations/path producers now use this converter directly or the inherited checked property. Scope is the Windows collection-path conversion flaw, not arbitrary separate filename arguments, filesystem symlinks or a universal clean counterpart. Sixteen functions still represent one CVE and stay grouped.

All four complete token issue/lookup/delete functions and the actual concealment helper inspected. _get_concealed_token constructs SHA-512 over HASH_PATH_PREFIX, token and HASH_PATH_SUFFIX, imported from Swift; local Swift token-object paths use that digest instead of the usable bearer token. This removes raw tokens from the affected storage request URIs and corresponding error-path strings. Scope is local token-object naming; the separate swauth_remote protocol, cache contents and every possible log site are not certified covered.

Full upload handlers plus validate_path_is_safe, _decode and is_file_uri inspected. The helper already repeatedly percent-decodes, converts file URIs and rejects parent segments, absolute paths and alternate separators before this commit; the change returns that validated representation and makes callers consume it. A rejected percent-encoded traversal is therefore not evidence that the old caller was exploitable. Still require the unchanged local_file_uri_to_path implementation and precise accepted-input/downstream interpretation discrepancy for CVE-2023-6976 before assigning a vulnerable-to-fixing function label. The public Huntr reference returned only its loading shell during this follow-up.

Full _list_artifacts and validation/decode helpers inspected. This read/list operation now retains the validator's returned canonical representation instead of the original path, but the preserved CVE description establishes arbitrary filesystem writing. Need a concrete call-chain/advisory link for this listing endpoint, as well as the accepted-input canonicalization discrepancy; sharing the upload-fix commit is insufficient attribution.

Complete multipart create/complete handlers and validation/decode helpers inspected. These callers retain the validator's returned artifact_path but separately pass request_message.path to backend multipart methods. The helper already rejects decoded parent/absolute paths. Need backend implementations and precise mapping of both path arguments to the CVE-2023-6976 filesystem-write mechanism before this can be called a vulnerable function and effective correction. No claim that these functions are irrelevant or still exploitable is made.

Complete selected functions, their fileio-to-artifact-store changes, BaseArtifactStore._register and all _sanitize_paths methods inspected. The replacement store resolves local paths but validates containment with raw startswith(root), without a path-component boundary. For root /srv/store a resolved /srv/store-other/file still passes. These callers therefore cannot be admitted as effective general artifact-store traversal fixes merely because they now use the decorated store. Most also concern materialization/output writes rather than the advisory-named step-log read endpoint. Reject the proposed fixing pairs, not the existence of CVE-2024-2083; no endpoint exploit was executed.

Full registration/notification callers, old and new hostname helpers, unchanged anchored regex and Matrix server-name parser inspected. This IPv6-compatibility commit replaces existing validation with a broader server-name validator or relocates optional-port validation to it. It does not introduce the missing validation or IP blacklisting described by CVE-2021-29431. As for previously reviewed queue 253, reject these compatibility pairs as the security correction.

Complete unbind servlet and changed exception branches inspected. The selected function adds a 400 response for InvalidServerName raised by the separately changed verifier and narrows a bare exception clause. It still delegates authentication in both versions; it does not itself validate the attacker-controlled origin before the outbound key request. This is error-reporting compatibility with the actual verifier fix, not a vulnerable SSRF sink or enforcement function.

Full _notify and exact-commit unchanged is_valid_hostname helper inspected at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matrix-org/sydent/8936925f561b0c352c2fa922d5097d7245aad00a/sydent/util/stringutils.py (decoded module SHA256 a193b8e16af7a924519ba77c6c884e0a5b9698ebf807b289d6a6ff70adc26707). New validation restricts hostname/port syntax before matrix:// construction, but this selected function sends onbind POST whereas the advisory specifies induced GET requests. Keep outside admission until that precise call-chain/scope attribution is established; syntactically valid internal hosts are still allowed here.

Complete registration caller and exact-commit imported helper source inspected. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/matrix-org/sydent/9e573348d81df8191bbe8c266c01999c9d57cd5f/sydent/util/stringutils.py has decoded module SHA256 6ce31b898c43073a33cb8b75b616b6d24fd9a0001ed927de5e6a153694db25d1; its valid_port parenthesized assignment lacks the closing parenthesis before except ValueError. The selected caller parses, but this companion does not establish a loadable fixing counterpart. Preserve this specific evidence problem rather than silently using a later repaired helper.

Complete client construction/configuration, default IP blacklist, generate_ip_set and the whole BlacklistingReactorWrapper/_IPBlacklistingResolver/check_against_blacklist chain inspected. DNS answers are withheld if a disallowed non-whitelisted address is returned, with private/local defaults and IPv4-mapped equivalents. Still require the actual Twisted Agent/endpoint behavior for numeric IP literals and the federation-client binding before claiming protection of all advisory-relevant GET routes. Defaults and resolver names alone do not settle those bypass/coverage boundaries.

All six complete multipart functions inspected against preserved GHSA-5m98-qgg9-wh84. The advisory explicitly identifies _read_chunk_from_length's EOF update as the minimum infinite-loop correction and describes this commit's form-data changes as additional handling fixes. The selected changes propagate subtype/default charset, change content decoding or outgoing serialization, handle _charset_, or reuse parsed boundary metadata; none adds the EOF/loop-termination correction. Reject these selected pairs as vulnerable-to-fixing examples of CVE-2024-30251, without rejecting the advisory's actual fix.

Complete custom-link and job-button renderers, grouped/error branches, HTML template constants and render_jinja2 binding inspected. Before, user-authored text and names were interpolated into HTML then mark_safe was applied to the whole result. After, format_html conditionally escapes each value; the changed render_jinja2 first strips django-jinja's implicit SafeString status so template-produced text cannot bypass that escaping. Preserve the exact helper with both callers. Scope is HTML text/attribute breakout in these features, not independent URL-scheme filtering or universal XSS freedom.

Full render_jinja2 before/after and actual custom-link/job-button consumers inspected. django-jinja's render result is implicitly marked safe; adding an ordinary string removes that status so the corrected format_html consumers escape user-authored rendered markup. This is a necessary trust-boundary correction for the advisory-named features, established with the complete consumers and their template constants preserved as companion modules. It is not claimed to sanitize markup or URLs by itself.

Complete upload functions inspected against the official CVE description and GHSA-wm83-3764-5wqh. Both explicitly identify 04cf68b45ebb5c03247a0d6453e35ffc175d55da as introducing the affected S3-proxy behavior; 2f6c5a883e106aa82a570d3d1f243993284b70f3 is the correction. These selected pairs belong to the introducing commit, including hostname proxying and extension-based disposition selection. They are not vulnerable-to-fixing examples; local storage changes are additionally outside the advisory's affected configuration.

Full signed-URL helper and serve_s3 caller inspected. The helper adds an optional ResponseContentDisposition=attachment parameter for forced downloads; with its default false value it generates the same get_object URL as before. The actual default-serving vulnerability is the filename-derived disposition overriding S3's content-type-aware stored header in serve_s3/nginx. This is support for the corrected forced-download API, not the vulnerable default response-selection operation.

Complete forced-download endpoint inspected with its serve_file consumer. The selected difference renames download=True to force_download=True while preserving the request to download an attachment. It neither contains nor corrects the unsafe default inline disposition; reject the API-forwarding compatibility pair for this CVE.

Full local-storage serving function inspected. It relocates extension-based attachment selection into the local backend after the shared/S3 paths stop using it. The advisory expressly excludes local-disk deployments from CVE-2023-22735; this compatibility change is not the affected S3 response path.

Complete serving callers, S3 upload/presigning helpers, MIME allowlist and both exact-commit nginx files inspected. Before, a .png filename could select inline even when the browser-supplied/stored content type was text/html. Upload already stores attachment disposition for types outside the allowlist, which excludes text/html. Corrected shared/token callers stop deciding from the extension; serve_s3 stops adding its own disposition, and nginx stops hiding S3's disposition. Forced downloads only override to attachment, and the nginx cache key includes that override. Preserve the non-Python configuration and unchanged MIME module by review-time byte hashes at this fixing commit. Scope is production S3 serving described by CVE-2023-22735, not local disk, every legacy stored object, or independently reproduced browser behavior.

Complete decorated get_json, client inheritance/registration binding, both changed callers and exact-commit response-reader module inspected. Previously readBody accumulated the remote homeserver response without a size limit. Registration now supplies 5 KiB and signing-key retrieval 50 KiB to this reader. It rejects oversized declared lengths and aborts chunked/unknown-length streams when accumulated bytes reach the supplied limit, ignoring further callbacks after failure. The default max_size=None remains unbounded: admission is conditional on the actual budgeted advisory-relevant callers, not all GETs. A received chunk is written before the accumulated-size check, so no exact peak-allocation bound is claimed. Scope is outgoing-response memory exhaustion, not incoming request/disk limits.

Complete post_json_get_nothing, exact-commit bounded-reader protocols and ThreepidBinder notification caller inspected. The caller constructs a federation onbind POST to the associated MXID homeserver; the response body is not consumed semantically. Previously readBody buffered the entire remote response merely to release the connection. The replacement uses a zero-byte budget and catches only BodyExceededMaxSize: declared nonempty responses are discarded/aborted and unknown-length responses abort on their first data chunk, instead of accumulating indefinitely. Other transport failures still propagate. This supports the advisory's broader malicious-homeserver response-exhaustion mechanism; it is not the separate incoming-request fix, a zero-allocation guarantee, or the GET-specific SSRF advisory.

Complete SevenZipFile.writestr and extraction path/helper changes inspected. This selected method writes new archive entries; it now checks arcname before delegating to _writestr. It does not read an attacker-supplied archive or constrain filesystem extraction. The CVE-2022-44900 advisory names crafted-archive extraction, whose corrective path resolution is in _extract/get_sanitized_output_path. Exclude this archive-creation hardening pair rather than label every changed function as the extraction vulnerability.

Complete SevenZipFile._extract, public extractall entry, worker dispatch and both path/link containment helpers inspected. Previously lexical relative_to accepted a path containing parent segments below the apparent prefix. The corrected helper resolves the candidate before relative_to; _extract supplies an absolute destination for relative roots and performs the check before registering files/directories for writes. This supports the crafted entry-name dot-dot traversal correction named by CVE-2022-44900. It does not certify race freedom or every link scenario: the separate link-target worker's default-root None handling remains quarantined at queue 612. The after-version is a scoped fixing counterpart, not universally clean code.

Complete Worker.extract_single before/after and Worker.extract/_extract_single callers inspected. The selected wrapper adds and forwards path while preserving file opening, seeking and exception dispatch. Actual destination validation is in _extract/get_sanitized_output_path and link-target enforcement in _extract_single/is_target_path_valid. This argument-forwarding compatibility pair is not itself a supported vulnerable containment operation merely because it shares the extraction fix.

Complete Worker._extract_single, is_target_path_valid and extractall -> _extract -> Worker.extract -> extract_single dispatch inspected. New symlink/junction checks resolve the link target before relative_to for explicit roots, but extractall's default path=None is forwarded unchanged to the helper, which immediately calls path.is_absolute(). This prevents establishing a functioning general default-root fixing counterpart. Retain the precise None-handling problem; do not silently substitute a later helper, assert an exploit was reproduced, or certify all extraction paths safe.

Complete collect_messages and old/new sessions/config modules inspected against GHSA-9w4w-cpc8-h2fq, which explicitly covers both linked CVEs. The selected difference supplies env to session construction and passes full expired-cookie records rather than names for removal. Session-cookie application and redirect sending are unchanged in this function. The domain-loss correction is in separate cookie serialization/accessors, not these environment/expiry API adaptations. Reject this selected pair as the vulnerable-to-fixing example, without rejecting either CVE.

Both complete BaseConfigDict load/save functions and Session pre_process_data/post_process_data, cookie accessors and materialize_cookie inspected. These generic JSON config methods add overridable processing hooks and version metadata support; base implementations return data unchanged. Domain retention is implemented by Session-specific cookie materialization and jar handling outside these selected methods. Exclude the generic hook/serialization infrastructure pairs rather than attribute the cookie-host vulnerability to every dependency of its fix. Legacy domainless sessions remain domainless with a warning unless explicitly upgraded; no automatic complete migration is claimed.

Complete generate_subparsers inspected against the session-cookie advisory. The changes copy argument/property dictionaries and unpack variadic option names while constructing the management CLI. There is no cookie persistence, domain restriction or redirect request in this selected function. Reject the management-parser compatibility pair.

Complete Session.__init__, get_httpie_session, cookie accessors, pre/post processing and materialize_cookie inspected. The constructor creates a jar and stores environment/session/bound-host metadata; the factory passes those fields and preserves session loading. bound_host is used by the migration warning, not to enforce a cookie domain. Actual persistence/accessor changes preserve domain metadata elsewhere, and old domainless sessions are warned about rather than automatically rebound. These selected state-construction/API pairs do not establish the vulnerable-to-fixing cookie-domain operation.

Complete update_headers and both session cookie representations inspected. This function parses explicitly supplied Cookie headers, which do not provide response Set-Cookie domain metadata. The replacement sets a default path and puts each Morsel in the jar without assigning the request host, while changing duplicate-header removal. It does not recover or preserve the domain lost when response cookies were serialized by the old cookies setter, the advisory's demonstrated persistent-session redirect leak. Reject this selected header-handling pair as that correction; no claim of general cookie-header safety is made.

Complete remove_cookies and its collect_messages expiry caller inspected. The change matches expired-cookie deletion by name/domain/path in the new jar rather than by name alone. It does not fix the old persistence operation that discarded response-cookie domains and leaked live cookies on redirects. Exclude this expiry/representation compatibility pair from vulnerable-to-fixing examples for the session-domain advisory.

Each complete multipart callback and the old/new parse, constructor and on_headers_finished implementations inspected against GHSA-74m5-2c7w-9w3x. These selected callbacks move part completion, header accumulation and part data from event messages into parser state; none counts parts or applies a maximum. Field/file counters and limit rejection occur in on_headers_finished before allocation. Exclude these event/state refactors as vulnerable-to-fixing examples of the unlimited-part-count flaw; no total-part-size or general memory-safety claim is made.

Complete old/new parse, callback registration, constructor and Request entry path inspected. Previously parser.write accumulated unbounded event messages and this function allocated files/items for every part without any count check. The corrected parse delegates allocation to on_headers_finished, whose counters raise MultiPartException before allocating the over-budget file/field; this exception propagates out of parser.write to Request._get_form. Finite defaults are 1000 files and 1000 fields, independently configurable. This supports the advisory's many-small/empty-parts DoS correction, not a bound on individual field/file bytes, a maximum for explicit infinite overrides, or complete cleanup of already-open files on exceptions.

Complete constructor, header-finished allocation/check callback, parser dispatch and Request entry inspected. Previously parser instances had no part-count policy or counters. The replacement establishes finite default max_files/max_fields of 1000 and initializes separate counters which on_headers_finished increments/checks before allocating the next part. Callback exceptions propagate through parse. This is the actual bounded-parser policy/state initialization, unlike unrelated event-storage refactors. Scope is finite configured part counts, not all multipart memory use or applications overriding limits with infinity.

All seven complete functions and imports inspected, followed by exact-commit requirements.txt and the pinned validators 0.19.0 URL/decorator source. The added public=True guard only rejects regex private_ip/private_host groups; its IPv6 alternative accepts loopback ::1 outside those groups. Hostname validation also does not resolve DNS, and pinned Requests 2.27.1 follows redirects by default while these callers do not disable/revalidate them. Thus the replacement is not an effective general internal-address SSRF boundary for the proposed fixing pairs, despite blocking literal localhost/selected IPv4 addresses. Exclude these attempted fixing counterparts; this is source reasoning, not an executed request, DNS probe or exploit. The dependency review retains exact release URLs/hashes and relevant excerpts.

Complete info main/get, GET-only function binding, unchanged call_if_user/call_if gate, issuer parser, typed configuration and deployment allowlist writer inspected. Previously main directly returned instance metadata. It now gates the extracted response callback through parse_jwt_token, whose missing/disallowed issuer Error causes HTTP 401 before the callback. Allowed issuers are exact sts.windows.net/<configured UUID>/ strings populated from deployment/admin configuration, not a token-selected list; the helper caches that list for 60 seconds. Admit for CVE-2021-37705's missing tenant authorization on this endpoint under the documented Azure-authenticated deployment boundary. jwt.decode still disables local signature verification; this is not a claim that arbitrary unverified tokens are cryptographically validated here or that revocation is instantaneous.

Complete decorated issuer-list helper, parse_jwt_token, actual endpoint gate and configuration/deployment chain inspected. The old parser returned UserInfo for Azure-accepted tokens from any tenant. The replacement rejects absent iss and issuers outside an exact list derived from stored allowed_aad_tenants UUIDs before returning UserInfo; call_if converts Error to HTTP 401 before invoking the endpoint. The model rejects absent/empty allowlists and normal deployment adds the deployment tenant plus explicitly configured tenants. Scope is tenant authorization after Azure token validation, not standalone signature verification; the 60-second allowlist cache and missing-config construction failure are not hidden by a universal operational-correctness claim.

Complete InstanceConfig.fetch, the shared model's required allowed_aad_tenants and root validator, and the real issuer gate inspected. This selected change supplies [] when constructing a missing configuration; the new root validator rejects that empty list, so it is not the functioning issuer-authorization operation. Existing valid tenant configuration is consumed elsewhere by get_allowed_tenants/parse_jwt_token. Exclude this missing-config construction/compatibility pair rather than label every change in the tenant-check commit as a vulnerable authorization function.

All three complete deployment/management functions and Client.set_instance_config/update_allowed_aad_tenants inspected. The selected main functions add CLI arguments and dispatch configuration updates; Client.__init__ stores the supplied tenant list. None processes a remote bearer token or decides issuer authorization. Exclude these deployment argument/state-plumbing pairs; preserve the actual configuration writer as companion evidence for the admitted runtime issuer/endpoint checks.

All six complete parsing/choice/template functions inspected, including previously truncated bodies, with DASourceError inheritance, server_error's role/debug-dependent source-error display branch, form html_validator bindings and make_safe_url changes in the same commit. These selected differences classify template/YAML/choice/variable errors as DASourceError, suppressing source details for ordinary users while retaining logging. They do not change field HTML validation or redirect URL normalization, the separately identified mechanisms for CVE-2024-27290/27291. Exclude these source-error disclosure/reporting pairs from those vulnerability/fix labels; no claim that arbitrary error rendering is universally XSS-free is made.

Each complete constructor and old HomeServer.get_http_client/new get_federation_http_client inspected. Both factory implementations construct the same MatrixFederationHttpClient with FederationPolicyForHTTPS; these selected changes rename that accessor in existing federation consumers. IdentityHandler's separately configured blacklisting_http_client is unchanged. The advisory's newly filtered key-validity and push operations instead switch from unfiltered SimpleHttpClient factories in queue 209/213. Reject these four accessor-rename compatibility pairs, without attributing every federation module change to those newly affected paths.

Full constructor, advisory-named third-party key-revocation GET consumer, client factory, configuration, numeric-IP wrapper, DNS filter and exact-commit ProxyAgent inspected. Previously the key URL used an unfiltered SimpleHttpClient. The new binding supplies config.ip_range_blacklist to a client that rejects listed literal IPs before dispatch and withholds DNS answers containing a listed IP on direct connections. This is a supported configured-policy correction for CVE-2021-21273. It requires the general denylist to contain the relevant private/local ranges: this commit defaults to only 0.0.0.0 and :: and does not migrate a federation-only list into the general list. Proxy-resolved target hostnames are not covered by the local resolver; no universal proxy/DNS-rebinding/secure-default claim is made.

Complete push constructor, URL provenance, both push/badge POST consumers, factory and full filtering chain inspected. The attacker-supplied pusher data URL previously used a proxied client without an IP policy; it now uses the configured general blacklist for literal targets and direct-connection DNS results. Preserve the exact ProxyAgent source, which distinguishes direct DNS from proxy-resolved hostnames. Admission is the configured-policy push correction named by CVE-2021-21273, not a claim that a missing general private-range list or a proxy doing its own target resolution is secured. Later default-policy improvements are not silently substituted into this fixing commit.

Complete federation-agent constructor, BlacklistingAgentWrapper signature/request and actual BlacklistingReactorWrapper class inspected. The new well-known wrapper is called as BlacklistingAgentWrapper(agent, self._reactor, ip_blacklist=...), but its second positional parameter is ip_whitelist. Thus the non-iterable reactor wrapper becomes the whitelist. For a listed literal IP, check_against_blacklist attempts membership in that object; the request wrapper catches the resulting exception in its broad 'not an IP' except and delegates the request. This added guard does not establish the intended literal-IP fixing counterpart. This is static argument/control-flow reasoning, not an executed request or reproduced exploit.

Complete MatrixFederationHttpClient constructor, both reactor implementations, agent constructor and request wrappers inspected. Existing DNS/literal-IP federation checks were already present; replacing the local Reactor with BlacklistingReactorWrapper preserves that policy and the other change forwards the blacklist into the new well-known wrapper. That wrapper misbinds its reactor as ip_whitelist and can bypass its literal-IP check through the broad exception handler, as recorded for queue 211. Exclude this refactoring/ineffective-helper counterpart; it is not the separately supported SimpleHttpClient push/key-validity correction.

Complete general/federation configuration loading and generated YAML inspected with both actual new runtime consumers and filtering helpers. The generated configuration supplies private/local ranges under the new general key, but read_config for an existing deployment defaults that key to [] and retains the old federation-only key separately; only 0.0.0.0 and :: are unconditional. Runtime client corrections are supported for explicitly configured ranges, but admission of these configuration-generation/loading functions as vulnerable functions still needs the actual generation/migration caller and deployment-specific before/after policy attribution. Do not report this commit as establishing private-range secure defaults for every upgrade.

Both complete token-authentication functions, Token.is_expired/accessed, UserObject.set_password, session loading and the real password-form commit inspected. Expired access tokens were already excluded before this commit. The selected changes return the matching token object, move last-access timestamp updates to the API caller and commit them; they do not revoke authenticated browser sessions after a password change. That CVE-2022-3362 correction is the separate SessionObject deletion in set_password plus its committed caller. Reject these token-activity/API adaptations as selected vulnerable-to-fixing examples; no general claim about token ownership or authentication safety is made.

All four complete persistence/transaction functions inspected together with UserObject.set_password, UserPasswordForm.populate_obj, Base.commit/flush and DbSession._load/_delete. Before, Base.add/delete committed by default and request teardown also committed; after, callers explicitly commit and teardown rolls back uncommitted work. DbSession._save preserves session persistence through add().commit(). None of these selected generic transaction operations identifies or invalidates another session after a password change; the actual revocation query is separately added to set_password and committed by its form caller. Exclude these compatibility/transaction-policy pairs from CVE-2022-3362 rather than label every dependency of the fixing commit.

Complete access-token creation and SSH-key addition, transaction helpers, password-change setter/form and session storage inspected. These selected differences adapt add/flush and rollback handling to the new explicit transaction API. They create tokens or authorized keys, not password changes or browser-session invalidation. Reject the two unrelated creation/persistence compatibility pairs as vulnerable-to-fixing examples of CVE-2022-3362.

Both complete enclosing/nested template functions, all helper bindings and Windows translation tables, plus exact-commit ExecPP.parse_cmd/run inspected against GHSA-hjq6-52gw-2g7p. The old %q branch used quote doubling, permitting the advisory's environment-variable expansion on Windows. It now calls shell_quote(value, shell=True), selecting percent-to-%%cd:~,% translation rather than the direct-argv table. ExecPP actually invokes prepare_outtmpl then substitutes its returned values before Popen.run(cmd, shell=True), establishing the documented shell path. Preserve the actual consumer and runtime command-extension/newline setup. These two overlapping functions represent one CVE and remain grouped. No exploit or Windows shell was executed; raw unquoted templates and arbitrary shell commands are not certified safe.

Both complete compatibility/argument-formatting functions and the new shell_quote tables/defaults inspected with actual %q and ExecPP callers. These selected wrappers call shell_quote without shell=True, selecting direct-argv Windows quoting rather than the percent-escaping cmd table. The affected %q path instead stops using compat_shlex_quote and explicitly selects shell=True in prepare_outtmpl. Reject these default-mode wrapper/representation changes as the CVE-2024-22423 percent-expansion correction; they are not certified suitable for arbitrary shell interpolation.

Complete Popen constructor/run, shell_quote tables and exact-commit ExecPP.parse_cmd/run inspected. The new shell_quote(args, shell=True) branch only runs for non-string arguments, while the advisory's actual --exec caller passes the already formatted command string. Its percent-expansion correction occurs in prepare_outtmpl/shell_quote before this constructor. The other constructor changes enable command extensions and supply the special newline-escaping environment variable; preserve them as runtime companion evidence, but exclude this selected list-quoting/runtime-support pair as the vulnerable %q interpolation correction. No Windows behavior was executed or universal shell-safety claim inferred.
